accounting.rationale: PDF125 line2 is the scalar lower/upper production, not a section-subscript triplet or vector-bounds production.
The defining specification-expr restrictions are read in10.1.11, not inferred from compiler acceptance.
PDF125 lines5-7: three alternatives yield upper-vector-only, two-vector and both scalar/vector mixed forms. R815/R816/R817 are not interchangeable with R819/C833.
Integer expression is the type production. C833 separately adds restricted-expression, rank-one and constant-size conditions; it does not require constant element values.
PDF125 lines9-10 gives a necessary context restriction for both bound forms, not blanket permission to use every form in every listed context.
R740/C754/C755 still require scalar explicit-shape-spec lists and component specification expressions for nonpointer nonallocatable array components.
Equal sizes are required, not equal element values, lower bounds of the bound-vector objects, or a vector/scalar size match.
PDF125 lines12-13 retains all four conjuncts, including constant size rather than constant values.
Rank determination is an observable property. The following scalar/array classification is accounted without a separate no-op classification requirement.
The entity is an explicit-shape array when the established rank is nonzero. This is not the same as its total size being nonzero.
A constant zero-size bound vector establishes rank zero and hence a scalar. A rank-one bound vector containing a zero upper bound instead establishes an array with a possibly zero extent.
PDF125 lines27-31 separates the permitted nonconstant bounds from their entry-time establishment and stability during the activation.

A named local explicit-shape array in the stated contexts may have nonconstant bounds, subject to its actual expression/role restrictions. This permission is not an extra executable case and does not waive C814 or C808.

requirements.title: A scalar explicit-shape specification has an upper bound and optional lower-bound colon
requirements.definition: Each scalar explicit-shape-spec supplies an upper-bound. Its lower-bound and following colon can be omitted together. The constituent bounds are specification expressions, not declaration strides or unrestricted vector expressions; R818 supplies the separate vector-bounds alternatives.

pending.declaration-stride-excluded: PENDING a complete declaration such as a(1:2:1,4), repaired by removing only the extra :1. Confirm that no R814/R818 alternative accepts that declaration. Require a source-bound declaration-bound/extra-colon cause, not generic EOF, missing END or unrelated section syntax.

requirements.oracle:
Grammar admissions and one minimally repaired, unambiguously malformed declaration candidate. A form that can instead be assumed-shape or assumed-size is not an R815 negative merely because an upper bound is absent.

Batch314 scalar explicit-shape syntax controls: one run/positive-control/f2023 program declares ordinary local INTEGER arrays with `a(4)`, `b(-2:1)` and `c(2,0:2)`. Direct LBOUND/UBOUND/RANK assertions distinguish the omitted lower bound, explicit scalar lower bound and two-entry scalar explicit-shape-spec list. Feature mutations replace the upper-only form by a same-extent explicit lower, shift the explicit lower range, or collapse the two-entry list to a rank-one declaration; all remain conforming and fail before the completion line.
requirements.oracle_limitation:
No prescribed fatal exit, diagnostic code or English wording. Unsupported vector/rank features, type errors elsewhere, source echoes, crashes, verifier failures and wrong-source recovery cannot establish the intended grammar condition.

Batch314 scalar explicit-shape syntax controls boundaries: Only scalar-list admissions with small default INTEGER bounds are covered; declaration strides, vector bounds and malformed alternatives remain pending.

A variable name in SIZE does not make the inquiry nonconstant. Do not import a global declaration-order diagnostic from this production.

requirements.oracle:
Complete scalar-bound contexts and source-specific canonical expression gates, with focused repaired controls for any proposed negative. The constancy of an inquiry is decided from the particular property inquired about.

requirements.title: A scalar upper bound is a specification expression
requirements.definition: The upper-bound nonterminal is a specification-expr, with the scalar integer, restricted-expression and applicable constancy/typing prerequisites of10.1.11 and10.1.12. This production neither requires positivity nor makes every bound expression constant.

pending.restricted-upper: PENDING a previously typed nonoptional non-INTENT(OUT) INTEGER dummy as upper bound in a subprogram. Specification-function candidates must be pure, noninternal, nonstatement and have no dummy procedure argument; do not merely add PURE to an internal function.
pending.prior-typing-inquiry: PENDING a constant-property inquiry such as SIZE of a prior fixed-shape array with constant bounds. Preserve C814_valid__automatic_save_size_constant and its compile/positive-control role rather than cloning or promoting it to a runtime effect.
pending.nonconstant-context-source-use: PENDING exact C831/10.1.11 context relation, separate from C833's rank-one restricted array expression with constant size. Any report/control policy must identify the actual upper-bound defect and retain canonical source ownership.

requirements.oracle:
Scalar integer specification-expression admission and exact type/expression-source relations; negative candidates have minimally repaired valid controls and case-specific causes.

Batch314 upper-bound specification control: one run/positive-control/f2023 program admits positive, zero and negative scalar INTEGER upper bounds with `positive(3)`, `zero(0:0)` and `negative(-3:-1)` and directly observes their upper bounds. Feature mutations change upper-bound values while preserving valid ranges, so the upper-bound assertions are load-bearing.
requirements.oracle_limitation:
No arbitrary kind IDs, constant-value assumption from initialization, implicit-type mismatch, unavailable inquiry, or unrelated generic kind/constant message. Ordinary scalar and vector upper-bound productions stay distinct.

Batch314 upper-bound specification control boundaries: Only scalar INTEGER upper-bound admissions are covered; restricted-function, prior-typing and context-source diagnostics remain pending.

requirements.title: Explicit vector bounds have four concrete scalar/vector combinations
requirements.definition: The first production permits an upper-bound vector alone or a lower-bound vector followed by an upper-bound vector. The other productions pair a scalar lower-bound with an upper-bound vector, or a lower-bound vector with a scalar upper-bound. R819/C833 govern vector expressions; R816/R817 govern scalar bounds. Component-array-spec has no corresponding vector-bounds alternative.

pending.upper-vector-only: PENDING ordinary INTEGER a([2,3]) admission as one vector-bounds specification, not a rank-one destination holding a descriptor.
pending.vector-pair: PENDING ordinary a([-1,2]:[1,5]) with two valid same-size bound vectors and fully specified prior declarations when names replace literals.
pending.scalar-lower-vector-upper: PENDING ordinary a(0:[1,2]), retaining the scalar specification-expression and the vector restricted/constant-size premises separately.
pending.vector-lower-scalar-upper: PENDING ordinary a([-1,1]:2), without falsely requiring the scalar to have the size of the vector.
pending.zero-size-vector-boundary: PENDING a prior rank-one INTEGER named constant of size zero used as the bound vector, including upper-only and same-size vector-pair forms. This declares a scalar, not a rank-one zero-extent array. No positive-size premise is added to C833 and no R740 component admission is inferred.

requirements.oracle: Complete conforming grammar admissions for the four combinations and zero-size boundary, with meaningful runtime property plans under p1/p3 rather than a no-op classification program.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Alternative parses must be resolved from the original grammar. Neither a vector placed where a scalar was expected nor a scalar paired with a vector is automatically invalid. No new compiler feature/profile assumption or duplicated canonical component case.

requirements.title: An explicit bound vector starts from an integer expression
requirements.definition: An explicit-bounds-expr is an int-expr. Its integer type is distinct from C833's rank-one, restricted-expression and constant-size requirements. Integer element values are not required to be constant or positive by this production.

pending.integer-expression-admission: PENDING default-INTEGER vector literal and previously typed INTEGER dummy-vector admissions in appropriate contexts. Other supported integer kinds are not excluded, but no kind identifier or narrowing conversion is assumed.
pending.noninteger-type-source: PENDING exact source relation for a REAL vector bound expression, with only its elements repaired to INTEGER values. This overlaps C833's integer condition: choose one canonical primary owner and a bound-expression type-specific report, not duplicate cases or generic kind text.
pending.c833-premises-source-use: PENDING finite separation of integer type from rank-one, restricted-expression and constant-size obligations. A scalar INTEGER bound can select R815 or a mixed R818 form and is not automatically a malformed vector expression.

requirements.oracle: Type-specific integer-expression admission/causal relation; C833 supplies the additional vector contract and keeps its own source ownership.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No fixed kind codes or compiler consensus. Do not credit an unsupported vector-bound facility, unrelated shape error, source echo or broad expected-integer recovery at another source point.

requirements.title: Nonconstant explicit bounds are restricted to four contexts
requirements.definition: An explicit-shape-spec or explicit-shape-bounds-spec with bounds that are not constant expressions occurs only in a subprogram, derived type definition, BLOCK construct or interface body. These contexts are necessary, not sufficient: the actual grammar, restricted/component expression, prior specification, initialization and SAVE conditions still apply.

pending.derived-type-nonconstant: PENDING a nonpointer nonallocatable array component with scalar-list bounds depending on a declared LEN type parameter. Apply R740/C754/C755 and10.1.11p9; a type parameter is not a variable. Do not use R818 vector bounds for the component merely because C831 names derived type definitions.
pending.interface-nonconstant: PENDING a complete interface body with explicitly typed dummy bound data and a compatible explicit-shape dummy/result declaration where permitted. The interface context does not establish runtime values or excuse result naming and procedure-characteristic rules.
pending.main-context-reporting-gate: PENDING candidate main-program declaration with use-associated nonconstant INTEGER bounds, repaired by replacing only those bound expressions with matching constants. Ordinary automatic variables also implicate implicit SAVE/C814 here. Hold fixture authoring until independent review establishes a C831-specific causal contract or a role-isolated context; do not duplicate C814 cases or credit a generic SAVE complaint as this condition.
pending.module-context-reporting-gate: PENDING the corresponding module-scope candidate with otherwise restricted, prior use-associated INTEGER bounds and constant-bound repair. Explicitly adjudicate the implicit-SAVE/automatic-object overlap and10.1.11 scalar-expression relation before any diagnostic fixture. No presumed uniquely isolated C831 negative or renewed C814 receipt.

requirements.oracle:
Four complete context admissions plus honest source-gated forbidden-context candidates with minimal constant-bound repairs. Source-defined constancy is tested by the particular expression/property, not by the presence of a variable token.

Batch314 explicit-shape context controls: one run/positive-control/f2023 program covers constant main/module bounds and nonconstant subprogram and BLOCK contexts. Module and main arrays use named constants; a subroutine declares `local(n)` from an INTENT(IN) dummy; a BLOCK declares `b(n)` from a host scalar defined before the BLOCK statement. SIZE assertions use independent literals. Feature mutations change the named constant, the subprogram actual, or the host scalar before BLOCK, all as conforming programs that fail the corresponding assertion.

C831 reporting capability is required, but no particular report format or fatal exit is mandated. The main/module candidates have a genuine C814 overlap requiring independent causal adjudication; unsupported facilities, unrelated type errors or general constant/SAVE nouns cannot stand in for that work.

Batch314 explicit-shape context controls boundaries: Only constant main/module, subprogram and BLOCK positive controls are covered. Derived-type, interface-body and forbidden main/module nonconstant diagnostics remain pending.

requirements.title: Two explicit bound vectors have equal sizes
requirements.definition: When an explicit-shape-bounds-spec contains two explicit-bounds-exprs, their sizes agree. This does not require equal element values or equal declared lower bounds of the vector objects, and it does not apply a two-vector size test to a scalar/vector mixed production.

pending.equal-vector-sizes: PENDING two rank-one INTEGER restricted vectors of size2 with different element values and different own declared lower bounds. Compare sizes, not vector index origins or values.
pending.unequal-vector-sizes: PENDING complete ordinary a([0,2]:[3]) with otherwise valid constant bound vectors, repaired only to a([0,2]:[3,4]). The causal report must concern unequal vector lengths; a rank, constancy, unsupported syntax or generic shape complaint is not sufficient.
pending.empty-vector-pair: PENDING two constant rank-one INTEGER vectors of size0; equal zero sizes are permitted and produce rank0. A size0 versus size1 candidate needs its same-size repair and the same exact size-mismatch cause.
pending.scalar-vector-boundary: PENDING the two R818 mixed forms, each with one scalar and one vector. There are not two explicit-bounds-exprs, so do not invent a size-one-equals-vector-size constraint.

requirements.oracle: Exact constant sizes in a focused two-vector mismatch/control pair, plus zero-size and scalar/vector boundary admissions.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No forced fatal status, message wording, arbitrary extent proxy or guessed kind. The source location and actual two-vector size relation must both be established; declaration recovery and unsupported facilities do not count.

requirements.title: An explicit bound vector is restricted, rank one, integer and constant-size
requirements.definition: An explicit-bounds-expr is a restricted expression that has rank one, integer type and constant size. Its element values need not be constant, and its constant size need not be positive. It is not the scalar specification-expr nonterminal; scalar/vector alternative parsing and the particular restricted-expression premises remain significant.

pending.rank-one-integer: PENDING complete ordinary entity declarations with a prior rank-one INTEGER bound vector. Small default-INTEGER values avoid representation assumptions; no blanket KIND=1/4/8 or byte-width inference.
pending.restricted-admission: PENDING INTEGER vector data from a prior nonoptional non-INTENT(OUT) dummy of fixed size, and a qualifying pure module specification function with explicit interface and fixed rank-one result size. All operations, primaries and source contexts must satisfy10.1.11.
pending.constant-size-not-values: PENDING ub(2) with differing defined values on separate valid calls, and SHAPE(W) after a prior W(m,n) whose rank is fixed and bounds are restricted. Constant vector size is distinct from constant values; preserve prior typing/specification conditions without treating every vector expression as the scalar R1029 nonterminal.
pending.zero-constant-size: PENDING a prior rank-one INTEGER named constant with size0 as the bound vector. Expect rank0 from p1, not an error for nonpositive vector length or a rank-one array with zero extent.
pending.rank-two-excluded: PENDING a prior rank-two constant INTEGER matrix used as the sole vector-bound candidate in an ordinary entity declaration, repaired only to a rank-one INTEGER vector with matching small values. The report must identify the bound expression's rank; rank-zero scalar syntax is not a substitute negative because another R818/R815 production can admit it.
pending.noninteger-owner-source: PENDING the precise R819/C833 shared INTEGER premise and one canonical REAL-vector diagnostic/control relation. No cloned duplicate type-negative under both owners or credit for unrelated integer/kind recovery.
pending.nonrestricted-function-excluded: PENDING an impure noninternal module function returning a fixed-size rank-one INTEGER vector, repaired only by making that otherwise qualifying function PURE. Keep its explicit interface, result size and body valid. Require the actual forbidden-function/restricted-expression cause; constant-value complaints are not valid substitutes.
pending.nonconstant-size-excluded: PENDING a subprogram with prior INTEGER dummy n and nonoptional INTENT(IN) INTEGER ub(n), then a(ub). C831 admits the context and ub is restricted, but its size is not constant. Repair only ub(n) to ub(2), with a compatible complete caller. Require the vector-size constancy cause, not a complaint that its allowed element values vary.

requirements.oracle: Independent checks of the four conjuncts, with focused minimal repairs for rank, nonrestricted function and nonconstant-size candidates, and one source-preserving canonical type relation.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No blanket demand for constant bound values, no rank-zero pseudo-negative that parses legally, and no ignored context/typing defect. Future causal contracts exclude broad kind/constant/expected strings, source echoes, unsupported language features, crashes, verifier failures and wrong-source recovery.

requirements.title: The list length or bound-vector size determines rank
requirements.source: 8.5.8.2 p1 rank clauses, physical PDF125, lines14-16
requirements.definition: The rank established by an explicit-shape-spec-list is its number of specifications. With explicit-shape-bounds-spec it is the size of a bound vector. A zero-size bound vector therefore establishes rank zero; a zero extent among an array's dimensions does not reduce that array's rank.

pending.vector-rank: PENDING direct RANK on a([2,3]) and corresponding mixed/pair forms, expecting rank2 independently of bound-vector element values and declared index origins.
pending.zero-vector-scalar: PENDING an entity declared using a prior constant zero-size INTEGER bound vector. Assign and read a defined scalar value, require RANK=0 and rank-one empty SHAPE, and do not directly call array-only SIZE/LBOUND/UBOUND on the scalar. A([0]) instead has rank1 and zero extent.

requirements.oracle:
Direct declared-object rank and legal shape/value checks with independent small literal expectations. The scalar/array classifications are not separate no-op programs.

Batch314 explicit-shape list-rank effect: one run/effect/f2023 program declares constant-bound explicit-shape arrays in a module and main program, including a zero-extent first dimension, and directly requires RANK=2 on the declared objects. The feature mutation changes the main two-specification list to one specification, so the direct rank assertion fails while the program remains conforming.
requirements.oracle_limitation:
No fixed-destination RANK, constructor proxy, corank substitution or compiler-derived expected value. Zero rank and zero total array size remain distinct; the argument contracts of every inquiry apply.

Batch314 explicit-shape list-rank effect boundaries: Only scalar explicit-shape-spec-list rank is covered. Vector-bounds rank and zero-size vector scalar behavior remain pending because the reference compiler rejects the F2023 vector-bound forms on this host.

requirements.title: Scalar bounds establish each dimension and an omitted lower bound is one
requirements.definition: The scalar lower/upper values establish the bounds and resulting extent of their corresponding dimension. An omitted lower bound is one. Bound inquiry results can normalize empty dimensions and expressions, so they are not unconditional echoes of the written bounds.
requirements.oracle:
Actual whole-array inquiries and defined element checks with literal bounds/extents in dimension order, after every allocation/association or argument premise applicable to the chosen object is satisfied.

Scalar explicit-shape bounds runtime fixtures: one complete run/effect/f2023 program declares three ordinary local INTEGER arrays with scalar explicit-shape-spec lists. `upper_only(4)` observes omitted lower bound one through LBOUND=[1], UBOUND=[4], SHAPE=[4], SIZE=4 and a nonzero whole-array payload. `explicit2d(-2:0,4:5)` observes dimension-order lower bounds [-2,4], upper bounds [0,5], shape [3,2], total size six and payload 52. `mixed(2,-1:1)` observes an omitted lower bound in only the first dimension, lower [1,-1], upper [2,1], shape [2,3], total size six and payload 63. Feature substitutions replace the upper-only declaration with a same-extent nonunit lower bound and remove explicit lower bounds from the other declarations, so default-lower and per-dimension lower-bound behavior are load-bearing rather than descriptor aliases.
requirements.oracle_limitation:
Use small representable INTEGER values, no kind-code folklore or descriptor-derived oracle. No illegal subscript or unallocated/disassociated bound inquiry is a negative twin for this effect.

Scalar explicit-shape bounds fixture boundaries: only scalar explicit-shape-spec-list effects on ordinary local INTEGER arrays are covered. This packet does not claim vector-bound syntax, rank-zero scalar vector-boundary behavior, dummy sequence association, function results, diagnostics, type parameters, storage layout, contiguity, coarrays, COMMON/EQUIVALENCE, allocation, pointer association or named-local nonconstant entry-capture semantics.

requirements.title: Vector position and element order determine bounds, with scalar broadcasting
requirements.definition: A vector immediately before the colon provides lower bounds; otherwise it provides upper bounds. Its elements correspond to dimensions in order. A scalar lower-bound or upper-bound in the vector production is used in every dimension. If lower bounds are absent, they are all one.

pending.vector-pair-order: PENDING a([-1,2]:[1,5]): require actual whole-array lower [-1,2], upper [1,5], shape [3,4], total12. Check defined dimension-specific values rather than another descriptor's shape.
pending.scalar-lower-broadcast: PENDING a(0:[1,2]): require lower [0,0], upper [1,2], shape [2,3], total6. Scalar and vector expression categories retain their different premises.
pending.scalar-upper-broadcast: PENDING a([-1,1]:2): require lower [-1,1], upper [2,2], shape [4,2], total8. Do not impose a two-vector equal-size condition on the scalar.
pending.omitted-lower-vector-default: PENDING a([2,3]): require lower [1,1], upper [2,3], shape [2,3]. Absence of a lower vector is not an inferred zero lower bound.
pending.vector-index-origin-independence: PENDING previously declared constant bound vectors with different own lower bounds, such as lower(-1:0)=[-1,2] and upper(4:5)=[1,5]. Expect the same a(lower:upper) bounds as the literal vector-pair plan; use first/second element order, not matching vector subscripts.

requirements.oracle: Independent literal rank, bounds, shape and size for all four R818 combinations, with defined data when inspected. Constant vector size and C832 agreement are established before the declarations.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No array-component vector syntax under R740, no rank/field/stride proxy, and no compile-only replacement for these runtime effects. Empty-dimension inquiry conventions are separate from bound-vector indexing.

requirements.title: Bound order determines inclusive or empty ranges and zero extents
requirements.definition: Either bound can be positive, negative or zero. When the upper bound is at least the lower bound, the dimension's valid subscripts run inclusively between them. Otherwise the range is empty, that dimension's extent is zero, and the array has zero total size.

pending.inquiry-normalization-source: PENDING exact whole-array versus array-expression/section and zero-extent LBOUND/UBOUND premises. Preserve their DIM/rank, assumed-size, allocated/associated and optional-argument restrictions; do not turn declaration bounds into a universal inquiry oracle.

requirements.oracle:
Finite valid range/extent effects using independently known integer bounds and direct inquiries on eligible objects. Empty arrays have no element-read or invalid-program twin.

Scalar explicit-shape range runtime fixtures: two complete run/effect/f2023 programs exercise scalar bound signs, inclusive nonempty ranges, singleton zero bounds and empty ranges. The range program declares positive_range(2:4), negative_range(-2:0) and zero_singleton(0:0), assigns nonzero whole-array payloads, observes bounds/shape/size and reads the actual lower and upper endpoint elements through LBOUND/UBOUND-derived subscripts. The empty program declares empty1(5:3) and empty2(5:3,-2:1), observes rank, normalized whole-array bounds, shapes [0] and [0,4], SIZE=0 for both, and a nonzero scalar path sentinel without reading any nonexistent element. Feature substitutions turn ranges into same-rank nonempty or default-lower declarations, so zero extent, inclusive range and bound-sign effects are distinguished while every mutant remains a conforming program.
requirements.oracle_limitation:
No negative-size allocation surrogate, unsigned arithmetic or guessed byte layout. Pure effects are not mandatory rejection tests, and empty extent does not authorize unallocated or disassociated inquiries.

Scalar explicit-shape range fixture boundaries: only valid scalar-list declarations with small default INTEGER bounds are covered. Empty arrays are observed only through permitted whole-array inquiries and a separate path sentinel; no element access, section inquiry boundary, assumed-size, optional dummy, allocation or processor diagnostic behavior is asserted. The separate inquiry-normalization-source facet remains pending.

requirements.title: Named local explicit bounds are captured on entry and remain stable during that activation
requirements.source: 8.5.8.2 p5 establishment and stability clauses, physical PDF125, lines27-31
requirements.definition: For a named local explicit-shape array of a subprogram or BLOCK construct with nonconstant bounds, evaluating the bound expressions on procedure entry or execution of BLOCK establishes the bounds and shape. Redefining or undefining variables during that procedure or construct does not alter those established bounds. This is not a global rule for every dummy, pointer, allocatable, result or coarray descriptor.

pending.vector-bound-capture: PENDING constant-size INTEGER lower/upper dummy vectors initially[-1,2]/[1,5], ordinary local a(lower:upper), then redefinition or controlled undefinition of those source vectors. Require literal captured lower[-1,2], upper[1,5], shape[3,4] and total12; do not use another descriptor constructed from the same changed vectors as oracle.

requirements.oracle: Two complete run/effect/f2023 programs implement only the first six facets. The procedure case declares an ordinary unsaved local INTEGER a(-2:n) after its nonoptional INTEGER INTENT(INOUT) n. Calls with incoming n=3 and n=1 supply independent scalar literal upper/extent/value expectations3/6/101 and1/4/102. The payload is assigned100+visit before inquiry. Each activation checks the actual whole array with LBOUND, UBOUND, SIZE, SHAPE and all-element value comparisons, first on entry, then after n=0, then after a separate plain INTEGER INTENT(OUT) helper leaves only n undefined and increments its distinct initialized event counter. No read of n occurs in that last window; n is restored from the independent upper expectation before return and checked again by main. Entry, change, undefinition, return and twenty-procedure-check-per-entry counts are independently consumed. The BLOCK case executes the same outer BLOCK twice with n=3/1, then takes nested inner bounds1:5/1:2 after redefining the host source. Distinct defined payloads201/202 and301/302, both arrays' actual bounds/shape/size, redefinition to9, inner exit and outer lifetime are checked with independent literal branch expectations. Main declares no array. Entry/exit/event/check counters and exact completion stdout, empty stderr and normal exit0 reject early-success/no-op behavior. Full-program one-span wrong-oracle probes address every guard, each repeated activation separately, and both completion literals, only on processors that execute the current complete parent.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Vector-bound-capture stays pending, and all twelve other explicit-shape requirements retain their source, plans and reviews. These are scalar R815-R817 bounds, not vector-bound syntax or copied S8.3 CHARACTER/type-parameter cases. The arrays are real named procedure/BLOCK locals, never array dummies, constructor RANK arguments, second expected descriptors, fixed destinations, allocatables, pointers, coarrays, COMMON/EQUIVALENCE objects or C interop storage. No SAVE, declaration/DATA/default initialization or escaped object masks their lifetime. Every payload is defined before inspection; only scalar independent observer inputs or literal branch expectations are used. The OUT helper neither reads nor defines the bound-source integer; all other actuals are distinct and defined, and restoration precedes the caller's next read. Inner arrays are never referenced after END BLOCK. Nonzero extents6/4 and5/2 make the whole-array inquiry bounds literal rather than zero-extent normalization cases. Runtime sensitivity requires completed builds, actual runtime and the intended unique guard/output failure; a compile rejection, unsupported facility, resource failure or crash is not a successful probe. ERROR STOP status/token behavior is empirically qualified, not a universal printed-code or numeric-status requirement. Source, fixture, native mode qualification and inventory adjudication remain separate; no approval, baseline, source-use or canonical-link renewal is added.

review_rationale: Batch314 bound reference-validated explicit- and assumed-shape fixtures after one review round; one frozen-LFortran failure (LBOUND of a zero-extent assumed-shape dimension) was independently confirmed as genuine; F2023 vector-bound forms remain pending because the reference compiler rejects them.
